11::D.attackDescription: Attacker fills the data store to capacity or corrupts its index causing all operations to fail
11::D.causeDescription: No redundancy for data store access — single point of failure
11::D.threatDescription: Data store unavailability — attacker makes the data store inaccessible

11::I.attackDescription: Attacker reads non-volatile memory to extract firmware, cryptographic keys, or sensitive configuration
11::I.causeDescription: Flash/EEPROM/NVRAM lacks readback protection — stored keys and credentials are readable
11::I.threatDescription: Embedded storage information disclosure — attacker reads sensitive data from non-volatile memory

11::R.attackDescription: Attacker accesses the data store and denies having done so because no log entry exists
11::R.causeDescription: No access logging on the data store
11::R.threatDescription: Data store access repudiation — access to the data store cannot be attributed

11::T.attackDescription: Attacker uses debug interface to modify firmware, configuration, or calibration data
11::T.causeDescription: Flash/EEPROM/NVRAM storage lacks access control or integrity protection
11::T.threatDescription: Embedded storage tampering — attacker modifies data in non-volatile memory

13::D.attackDescription: Attacker blocks or corrupts the data flow causing dependent components to lose communication
13::D.causeDescription: No redundancy or timeout protection — disruption causes loss of communication
13::D.threatDescription: Data flow disruption — attacker blocks or delays the data flow

13::I.attackDescription: Attacker passively monitors the data flow and captures sensitive data
13::I.causeDescription: Data flow is unencrypted — sensitive payload is transmitted in plaintext
13::I.threatDescription: Data flow eavesdropping — attacker intercepts sensitive data on the data flow

13::T.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts and modifies values before they reach the destination
13::T.causeDescription: Data flow is unprotected — no integrity check or encryption prevents modification
13::T.threatDescription: Data flow tampering — attacker modifies data in transit between components

15::D.attackDescription: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability
15::D.causeDescription: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed
15::D.threatDescription: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack

15::E.attackDescription: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication
15::E.causeDescription: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed
15::E.threatDescription: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach

15::I.attackDescription: Attacker measures power consumption or EM emissions and extracts cryptographic keys
15::I.causeDescription: Physical boundary provides no electromagnetic shielding — internal operations are observable
15::I.threatDescription: Side-channel observation — sensitive data extracted via physical measurements

15::T.attackDescription: Attacker opens the enclosure without triggering any alarm, gaining access to internal components
15::T.causeDescription: No tamper detection mechanism — unauthorized opening is undetected
15::T.threatDescription: Physical boundary tampering — unauthorized physical access to boundary interior

16::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits embedded process debug interface to execute code with elevated privileges
16::E.causeDescription: Debug interface or privileged API accessible without proper authentication
16::E.threatDescription: Embedded process privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated access on embedded process

16::I.attackDescription: Attacker captures power traces during cryptographic operations and recovers the secret key via DPA
16::I.causeDescription: No power analysis countermeasures on chip — key-correlated power signature is measurable
16::I.threatDescription: Power side-channel attack — cryptographic key extracted via differential power analysis

16::T.attackDescription: Attacker loads malicious firmware that bypasses Secure Boot verification
16::T.causeDescription: Secure Boot is not enforced — unsigned firmware can execute
16::T.threatDescription: Secure Boot bypass — attacker bypasses cryptographic boot chain verification

17::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
17::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
17::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

17::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
17::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
17::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

17::I.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
17::I.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
17::I.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

17::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
17::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
17::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

17::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
17::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
17::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

17::T.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
17::T.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection
17::T.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface

19::R.attackDescription: External entity denies having sent a command that the system received and acted upon
19::R.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism — requests from external entities are not cryptographically bound to the sender
19::R.threatDescription: External entity repudiation — external entity denies having sent a request

19::S.attackDescription: Attacker crafts requests that appear to originate from a legitimate external entity
19::S.causeDescription: No authentication mechanism enforced for external entities
19::S.threatDescription: External entity identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate external entity

21::D.attackDescription: Attacker blocks or corrupts the data flow causing dependent components to lose communication

21::D.threatDescription: Data flow disruption — attacker blocks or delays the data flow

21::I.attackDescription: Attacker passively monitors the data flow and captures sensitive data

21::I.threatDescription: Data flow eavesdropping — attacker intercepts sensitive data on the data flow

21::T.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a hardware probe to the embedded bus and injects or modifies transmitted data

21::T.threatDescription: Embedded bus data tampering — attacker modifies communication on internal bus

3::D.attackDescription: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles
3::D.causeDescription: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests
3::D.threatDescription: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service

3::R.attackDescription: Process or its operator denies having executed a command that affected the system

3::R.threatDescription: Process action repudiation — process denies having performed an action

3::T.attackDescription: Attacker replaces embedded process firmware to disable security checks or introduce a backdoor

3::T.threatDescription: Embedded process firmware tampering — attacker modifies firmware of embedded process component

5::S.attackDescription: Attacker crafts requests that appear to originate from a legitimate external entity

df::13::D::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts or delays the response channel from Flash, causing MyProcess to stall or fail
df::13::D::outgoing.causeDescription: No redundancy or timeout protection — MyProcess depends on responses from Flash to continue operation
df::13::D::outgoing.threatDescription: Response blocking: Attacker prevents MyProcess from receiving responses from Flash

df::13::E::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the response from Flash to include elevated roles or permissions, causing MyProcess to grant unauthorized access
df::13::E::outgoing.causeDescription: MyProcess trusts response data from Flash without integrity verification, enabling privilege decisions based on forged responses
df::13::E::outgoing.threatDescription: Response manipulation for privilege escalation: Attacker manipulates response to gain elevated access in MyProcess

df::13::I::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Flash to MyProcess and reads sensitive information
df::13::I::outgoing.causeDescription: Unencrypted or weakly protected response channel — response data is readable in transit
df::13::I::outgoing.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on response: Attacker intercepts sensitive response data from Flash

df::13::R::outgoing.attackDescription: Flash claims it never received the data from MyProcess, or denies having processed it
df::13::R::outgoing.causeDescription: No delivery confirmation or cryptographic receipt — MyProcess has no proof that Flash received its data
df::13::R::outgoing.threatDescription: Receiver repudiation: Flash denies receiving or processing the request

df::13::S::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker sets up a rogue endpoint pretending to be Flash, causing MyProcess to send sensitive data to the attacker
df::13::S::outgoing.causeDescription: Missing endpoint validation before data transmission — MyProcess cannot verify the true identity of the receiving endpoint
df::13::S::outgoing.threatDescription: Receiver spoofing: Attacker impersonates Flash to intercept data from MyProcess

df::13::T::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Flash and modifies data, causing MyProcess to process falsified information
df::13::T::outgoing.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the response flow from Flash — MyProcess cannot detect modified responses
df::13::T::outgoing.threatDescription: Response tampering: Attacker modifies response data before it reaches MyProcess

df::21::D::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker sends a high volume of requests via the data flow, exhausting the processing capacity of STM32F4 [STM]
df::21::D::incoming.causeDescription: No rate limiting or request throttling protecting STM32F4 [STM] from high-volume input via Debugger
df::21::D::incoming.threatDescription: Request flooding: Attacker overwhelms STM32F4 [STM] with excessive incoming requests

df::21::E::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker injects malicious commands or payloads into the data flow, which STM32F4 [STM] executes with its own privilege level
df::21::E::incoming.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation in STM32F4 [STM] — incoming data from Debugger is processed with elevated trust
df::21::E::incoming.threatDescription: Command injection: Attacker injects commands via data flow to escalate privileges in STM32F4 [STM]

df::21::I::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker passively monitors the data flow and reads sensitive payload transmitted from Debugger to STM32F4 [STM]
df::21::I::incoming.causeDescription: Unencrypted or weakly protected communication channel between Debugger and STM32F4 [STM]
df::21::I::incoming.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on incoming data: Attacker intercepts sensitive data flowing to STM32F4 [STM]

df::21::R::incoming.attackDescription: Debugger claims it never sent the command or data that STM32F4 [STM] received and acted upon
df::21::R::incoming.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from Debugger are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender
df::21::R::incoming.threatDescription: Sender repudiation: Debugger denies sending the request or data

df::21::S::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker forges the identity of Debugger and sends malicious data to STM32F4 [STM], which processes it as legitimate
df::21::S::incoming.causeDescription: Missing sender authentication on incoming data flow — STM32F4 [STM] cannot verify the true origin of received data
df::21::S::incoming.threatDescription: Sender spoofing: Attacker impersonates Debugger to deceive STM32F4 [STM]

df::21::T::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the data flow from Debugger and modifies commands or payload before delivery to STM32F4 [STM]
df::21::T::incoming.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the data flow from Debugger — data arrives without tamper evidence
df::21::T::incoming.threatDescription: Data tampering on incoming flow: Attacker modifies data before it reaches STM32F4 [STM]

df::7::R::incoming.attackDescription: MyExternal claims it never sent the command or data that MyProcess received and acted upon
df::7::R::incoming.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from MyExternal are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender
df::7::R::incoming.threatDescription: Sender repudiation: MyExternal denies sending the request or data

df::7::R::outgoing.attackDescription: MyProcess claims it never received the data from MyExternal, or denies having processed it
df::7::R::outgoing.causeDescription: No delivery confirmation or cryptographic receipt — MyExternal has no proof that MyProcess received its data
df::7::R::outgoing.threatDescription: Receiver repudiation: MyProcess denies receiving or processing the request

df::7::T::incoming.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the data flow from MyExternal and modifies commands or payload before delivery to MyProcess
df::7::T::incoming.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the data flow from MyExternal — data arrives without tamper evidence
df::7::T::incoming.threatDescription: Data tampering on incoming flow: Attacker modifies data before it reaches MyProcess

df::7::T::outgoing.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from MyProcess and modifies data, causing MyExternal to process falsified information
df::7::T::outgoing.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the response flow from MyProcess — MyExternal cannot detect modified responses
df::7::T::outgoing.threatDescription: Response tampering: Attacker modifies response data before it reaches MyExternal

el::15::D.attackDescription: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability
el::15::D.causeDescription: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed
el::15::D.threatDescription: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack

el::15::E.attackDescription: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication
el::15::E.causeDescription: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed
el::15::E.threatDescription: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach

el::15::I.attackDescription: Attacker measures power consumption or EM emissions and extracts cryptographic keys
el::15::I.causeDescription: Physical boundary provides no electromagnetic shielding — internal operations are observable
el::15::I.threatDescription: Side-channel observation — sensitive data extracted via physical measurements

el::15::T.attackDescription: Attacker opens the enclosure without triggering any alarm, gaining access to internal components
el::15::T.causeDescription: No tamper detection mechanism — unauthorized opening is undetected
el::15::T.threatDescription: Physical boundary tampering — unauthorized physical access to boundary interior

el::17::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
el::17::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
el::17::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

el::17::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
el::17::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
el::17::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

el::17::I.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
el::17::I.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
el::17::I.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

el::17::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
el::17::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
el::17::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

el::17::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
el::17::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
el::17::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

el::17::T.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
el::17::T.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection
el::17::T.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface

el::9::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
el::9::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
el::9::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

el::9::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
el::9::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
el::9::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

el::9::I.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
el::9::I.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
el::9::I.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

el::9::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
el::9::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
el::9::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

el::9::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
el::9::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
el::9::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

el::9::T.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the maintenance interface outside any scheduled window
el::9::T.causeDescription: Interface declared maintenance-only but no policy enforcement disables it outside windows
el::9::T.threatDescription: Maintenance interface accessible outside maintenance window — unauthorized privileged access at any time
